answer.rationale: The 18% cut is mandatory and the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferring is not viable. Switching primary vendors or adding a second source introduces delivery risk at 94% utilization with no buffer, which the primary objective explicitly forbids. Renewing the incumbent at status quo does not meet the 18% reduction. Negotiating terms at renewal is the only direction that addresses cost while preserving the existing, stable supply relationship and delivery cadence. memory_c4 (benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms) and memory_c6 (multi-year commitment with the incumbent unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope) are the two most directly relevant precedents: both show that cost reduction can be extracted from an incumbent renewal without increasing delivery risk. Verifying both will confirm whether those outcomes were durable and whether the levers used are still applicable under a tighter 18% target.
